experiment: T1 temporal misalignment (stale image + current alignment), k=1..5
platform: AutoDL instance, RTX 3090, PyTorch 2.1.0 / CUDA 12.1 / Python 3.10 (conda env bevfusion)
dataset: nuScenes v1.0-trainval, val split, 6019 keyframe samples

definition.substitution: 6 camera images replaced by real historical frames k steps back along sample_data.prev; calibration, poses, LiDAR and GT of the current sample kept unchanged
definition.ineligible_samples: scene-first frames without k predecessors in scene
definition.note: eligible sets k1-k4 identical; k5 loses 6 more samples (scenes too short). Paired common subset across all settings = 5863.

conclusions: No backfire yet, but the fusion-vs-lidar gap closes to +0.64pt mAP / +0.13pt NDS at k5 (mean 423ms); linear trend suggests crossover around k~7 (+/-2), i.e. ~0.6-0.9s misalignment.
mATE peaks at k3 (0.2898) then regresses toward the LiDAR-only level at k4/k5; mAOE keeps rising — very stale images stop adding usable geometric signal and behave increasingly like LiDAR-only.
Next round should probe k=6..8 (and maybe 10) to locate the actual backfire threshold.
known_limitations: k3/k4 cumulative predictions cover 5865 tokens (4 tokens short of the 5869 eligible) because the backfill pass required k5-eligibility; the paired table is unaffected since k5 caps the common subset at 5863.
Single GPU/environment (AutoDL RTX 3090); cross-GPU reproducibility comparison pending other members' runs.
